films.title: Brambling
article: Brambling is a 2024 British drama written and directed by Mirela Voss. Set on a failing hedge nursery in the Fens, it follows two sisters through a single wet autumn.

Cinematographer Tobiah Okafor, who shot Lantern Season on the Alexa Mini, chose the Sony Venice 2 for Brambling because he wanted the latitude of its dual base ISO. Principal photography ran for thirty-one days in Cambridgeshire and Norfolk. The film was composed for 2.39:1 and the trailers were cut at 1.85:1.

films.title: The Saltmarrow Hours
article: The Saltmarrow Hours is a 2023 coastal mystery film directed by Ines Calloway. It was shot by Ruth Adebayo-Lind on Kodak Vision3 500T 5219 and 250D 5207 stocks, processed at Kodak Film Lab London.
The film was released theatrically at 1.85:1. A rumoured IMAX version of the storm sequence was never confirmed by the studio.

films.title: Undertow Parish
article: Undertow Parish is a 2021 drama directed by Mateus Kerridge and set in a flood-threatened village in the Somerset Levels. Ruth Adebayo-Lind photographed the film.
The camera package was supplied by Panavision London. The end credits list Lotte Brenner as Steadicam operator and Amara Quell as dolly grip.
It was finished at 2.39:1, extracted from the Mini LF’s open-gate 3:2 capture.

films.title: …And the Orchard Burned
article: …And the Orchard Burned is a 2025 period drama directed by Ferran Quist. It is set in an apple-growing valley in 1911.
Cinematographer Halvard Mbeki lit the farmhouse interiors with dimmed halogen bulbs inside hurricane lamps, emulating candlelight without the flicker problems of open flame.
The film was shot on the ARRI Alexa 35 in its 4:3 mode with Hawk V-Lite anamorphics, and released at 2.39:1.

films.title: Winter’s Ledger
article: Winter’s Ledger is a 2022 legal drama directed by Odile Fenwick. It follows a provincial accountant who becomes a witness in a fraud trial.
Casimir Tran photographed the film on 16mm, using Kodak Vision3 7219 for interiors and 7213 for exteriors.
The film was framed for 1.66:1 on the Super 16 negative. Its streaming release was cropped to 1.78:1, a decision Fenwick has criticised.

films.title: Lowtide — A Fugue
article: Lowtide — A Fugue is a 2024 experimental drama directed by Bastian Orrell. Its four movements take place on the same Breton beach across a single tide cycle.
Cinematographer Yuki Delacroix-Hart shot the film on the Sony Burano with Leitz Hektor primes. The second movement switches to a 1.33:1 frame for its entire twelve-minute length.
A camera car fitted with a Russian Arm carried the Burano along the sand for the opening shot.

films.title: Pennyroyal
article: Pennyroyal is a 2021 Irish horror film directed by Saoirse Lund. Marek Obuya shot it on the RED Komodo 6K, often mounted on a DJI Ronin 2.
The title sequence was shot through a Lensbaby Composer, an effect Obuya first used on his short Kettle Psalm. Pennyroyal was distributed at 2.00:1.

films.title: Cinderwick
article: Cinderwick is a 2025 fantasy adventure directed by Anouk Brannigan. It was photographed by Teodor Ashworth in large format on the ARRI Alexa 65 with Prime DNA lenses.
Theatrical exhibition was at 1.90:1 in IMAX venues and 2.39:1 elsewhere. The 4K disc presents the film at 2.39:1 only.
The credits name Dov Arnesen as Technocrane operator and Saffi Rhee as drone pilot.

films.title: The ‘Gannet’ Tapes
article: The ‘Gannet’ Tapes is a 2023 found-footage thriller directed by Lior Castellane. Its premise is that the footage was recovered from a seabird researcher’s equipment.

Although the film is presented as Hi8 video, Wren Halvorsen actually shot it on a Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 6K and applied a Hi8 emulation in the grade. The 4:3 frame was extracted from the camera’s 16:9 sensor area.

films.title: Driftglass
article: Driftglass is a 2022 romantic drama directed by Tomasz Ellery, set among beachcombers on the Northumberland coast. Wren Halvorsen shot the film on a Panavision Millennium DXL2 with Primo 70 lenses.
The film was released at 2.39:1, framed within the DXL2’s full-frame sensor.

films.title: Moth Parliament
article: Moth Parliament is a 2024 political drama directed by Kwabena Stroud. Elif Marchetti shot it on the ARRI Alexa 35 with Zeiss Supreme Prime Radiance lenses.
Its distinctive silver look is often mistaken for bleach bypass, but it was created digitally.

films.title: Quarry Light
article: Quarry Light is a 2022 drama about a family of stonemasons, directed by Delphine Arkwright. Oskar Nyambura shot the film on Kodak Vision3 50D 5203 and 250D 5207 with a Panavision Millennium XL2.
The film was captured in 3-perf Super 35 and framed for 2.39:1. Its 2026 4K restoration from the original negative keeps the 2.39:1 frame.

films.title: Tinderbox Psalm
article: Tinderbox Psalm is a 2025 drama directed by Hollis Varga. Priya Lindqvist shot it on the Sony Venice 2 with Cooke S7/i Full Frame Plus primes.
Unlike Varga’s previous film, Ninefold, which was shot on 35mm with Panavision C-Series anamorphics, Tinderbox Psalm is spherical and digital.

films.title: Ash & Lanolin
article: Ash & Lanolin is a 2024 rural drama about sheep farmers in the Welsh borders, directed by Petra Szabo-Quinn. It was shot by Callum Ferreira-Holt on Super 16 with an Aaton Xtera and Kodak Vision3 7219.
The film was projected at 1.66:1 in cinemas, and a 2025 streaming remaster retained that frame.

films.title: Starling Debt
article: Starling Debt is a 2023 crime drama directed by Rhiannon Achterberg. Jovan Pelletier shot the film on a Red V-Raptor 8K VV with Leica Thalia lenses.
Reports that the car chase was shot with an IMAX camera are unfounded, according to Pelletier. Its theatrical aspect ratio was 2.39:1, extracted from a 17:9 capture.

films.title: Halfway to Oxbow
article: Halfway to Oxbow is a 2025 American road movie directed by Imre Castellanos. Greer Abernathy shot it on the ARRI Alexa Mini LF and an Alexa 35, with a set of rehoused Canon K35s.
The film was shot open gate and finished at 2.39:1 for theatrical release, with a 1.90:1 version for IMAX venues. Its Alexa 35 cameras were supplied by ARRI Rental.

films.title: Copperhead Vespers
article: Copperhead Vespers is a 2024 Southern Gothic thriller directed by Nell Okonkwo-Barr. Ansel Ruiz-Tamm photographed it on Kodak Vision3 500T 5219, which he pushed one stop for the night revival scenes.
Ruiz-Tamm has said he reaches for Kodak Double-X 5222 whenever a project calls for black and white.

films.title: A Map of Sleeping Dogs
article: A Map of Sleeping Dogs is a 2023 Finnish-South African co-production directed by Florian Mbatha. Kirsi Hallward shot it on the Sony Venice with Atlas Orion anamorphic lenses.
The film was framed for 2.39:1, but its Blu-ray release is presented at 1.78:1 from an open-matte transfer.

films.title: Glasswort
article: Glasswort is a 2021 coming-of-age film directed by Esme Varadi and set on a salt marsh in Essex. Theo Lindgren-Achebe shot it on 35mm with an Arricam ST and Cooke S4/i lenses.
The film was captured in 4-perf and released at 1.85:1. A 2026 4K restoration supervised by Lindgren-Achebe reframed the film to 2.00:1 for a festival re-release.

films.title: Paper Lanterns, Iron Bells
article: Paper Lanterns, Iron Bells is a 2025 historical epic directed by Ruben Castile. Maren Tull shot the film on the ARRI Alexa 65 and on IMAX 15/65mm film for six key sequences.
Those sequences open up from 2.39:1 to 1.43:1 in IMAX 70mm exhibition.

pages.title: Wet Season: Tobiah Okafor on Brambling
paragraphs: Tobiah Okafor spent most of Brambling soaked. The nursery set, a cluster of real polytunnels outside Ely, flooded twice during the shoot, and the camera team learned to work in waders.

Okafor paired the Venice 2 with a set of Cooke Panchro/i Classic primes, which he describes as forgiving on skin and unkind to everything else. Unlike Glasshouse Weather, which Okafor shot entirely on Kodak Vision3 500T 5219, Brambling never went near celluloid.
“People assume we used a Black Pro-Mist, but there is no filtration on the lens at all,” Okafor says.
The polytunnels were lit from outside with Aputure LS 1200d Pro units pushing through the plastic, while a pair of ARRI SkyPanel S60-Cs rigged inside carried the night scenes.

A Super 8 camera that the younger sister carries everywhere is a prop from a Bury St Edmunds junk shop and was never loaded. The film’s two flashbacks were handled differently, one in 16mm and the other on Super 8, both scanned at Cinelab London.
Voss had originally wanted to shoot anamorphic, but the idea was abandoned after a budget cut in pre-production. “In the end I think spherical suited the sisters better,” she says.

pages.title: Three Grades: Ilse Marrow on Brambling, Moth Parliament and Ash & Lanolin
paragraphs: Colorist Ilse Marrow has had an unusually busy eighteen months. We asked her to walk us through three recent features, all graded in her room in Soho.
Brambling

On Brambling, Marrow built a print-film emulation LUT in DaVinci Resolve so that the Venice 2 footage would sit closer to the 16mm flashbacks. Nothing in the main body of the film was printed to Kodak 2383; the print look is entirely emulated.
Moth Parliament

On Moth Parliament, Marrow worked from ARRIRAW originated on an Alexa 35, with the cinematographer’s own show LUT as the starting point. The silvery, crushed-shadow look that critics called bleach bypass was an emulated ENR built in Resolve; no film was ever processed. Bleach bypass is a laboratory process in which the bleach step is skipped so that silver remains in the emulsion alongside the dyes.
Ash & Lanolin
On Ash & Lanolin, the brief was the opposite: a 16mm negative, scanned on a Scanity, with almost nothing done in the grade.

pages.title: Salt and Shadow: A Conversation with Ruth Adebayo-Lind
paragraphs: Ruth Adebayo-Lind has photographed features for Ines Calloway and Mateus Kerridge. We spoke between prep days on her next project.
AC: Let’s start with The Saltmarrow Hours. Why film?
Adebayo-Lind: Ines wanted grain that moved. We carried an Arricam LT for most of it and an Arriflex 235 for the handheld days on the causeway.
AC: Any diffusion?
Adebayo-Lind: Nothing except a Tiffen Glimmerglass 1 on the night interiors, so no Pro-Mists, no nets and no Hollywood Black Magic.
AC: Was the day-for-night material on 5203?
Adebayo-Lind: I’m honestly not familiar with that stock by number. The loader placed the orders, and I asked for the slowest daylight film we could get.
AC: And on Undertow Parish, a couple of years earlier?
Adebayo-Lind: That one was all digital, an Alexa Mini LF with Signature Primes. We never shot a frame of 35mm on it, though people still ask because of the texture.
AC: Back to Saltmarrow: the lighthouse scene reads as pure moonlight.
Adebayo-Lind: It’s a 20K tungsten Fresnel up on a Condor, gelled full CTB, plus a lot of smoke.
AC: If you were to shoot it again?
Adebayo-Lind: I’d probably take the Alexa 65 out for the storm, just to see what the sensor does with spray.

pages.title: The Saltmarrow Hours
paragraphs: Cinesite delivered 142 visual effects shots for The Saltmarrow Hours, led by the storm sequence and the lighthouse collapse.

Plates were captured on the production’s Arricam LT and scanned at 4K before our compositors extended the sea stacks. Because the practical 18K HMI on the clifftop could not reach the water, the team built a digital beam that matched its throw.
Our environment team also rebuilt the harbour wall, which was demolished a year before the shoot.

pages.title: Flood Light: Lighting Undertow Parish
paragraphs: For the church sequence in Undertow Parish, Adebayo-Lind and gaffer Joss Penhale wanted the light to feel as if it came off the water.

They floated two LiteGear LiteMat 4s on rafts in the flooded nave and bounced a Creamsource Vortex8 off a silver sheet rigged under the gallery. The Vortex8 can run from a V-mount battery for roughly an hour at full output, which made the rafts possible.
Penhale says he carries a pair of Astera Titan Tubes on every job for exactly this kind of emergency.
The DJI Ronin 4D that appears in behind-the-scenes photos belonged to the EPK crew, not the main unit.

pages.title: First Light: Three Debut Features
paragraphs: Debut features rarely get the prep time their cinematographers want. These three found ways around it.
…And the Orchard Burned

Mbeki tested the Alexa 35 against a Venice 2 and a Red V-Raptor in the orchard at dusk, and the Alexa won on the highlight roll-off in the blossom. The fire was lit for real with a controlled burn on the last two nights, supplemented by flicker boxes driving Quasar Science Rainbow 2 tubes.
Winter’s Ledger

On Winter’s Ledger, Casimir Tran went the other way, shooting 16mm on an Arriflex 416 with Zeiss Ultra 16 primes. Tran says one of his decisions was never to use a zoom, even for the long-lens courtroom coverage.
Lowtide — A Fugue

For Lowtide — A Fugue, Yuki Delacroix-Hart, whose previous feature was shot on Ektachrome reversal, stayed digital with a Sony Burano. The beach material was shot at 48 frames per second and played back at 24.

pages.title: …And the Orchard Burned
paragraphs: Cinesite’s team created the orchard fire extensions for …And the Orchard Burned.
Plate photography used a Technocrane on a tracked base so that the burning rows could be revisited with matching moves.
A DJI Inspire 3 carried a Zenmuse X9 for aerial plates over the valley.

pages.title: Gaffer Notes: Noor Castellan
paragraphs: Noor Castellan had never lit a fire scene before …And the Orchard Burned.
For the barn sequence she rigged twelve Maxi-Brutes on the hillside behind the trees. The barn interior, by contrast, was lit with

pages.title: Why Casimir Tran Keeps Coming Back to Sixteen
paragraphs: Casimir Tran shoots more 16mm than almost anyone working in features today.
He says he always carries an Arriflex 416 and a Bolex as a crash camera, whatever the production.
On Winter’s Ledger the Bolex never came out of its case.
Winter’s Ledger’s courtroom was lit with a single 12K HMI through a 12×12 Ultrabounce, with Kino Flo Celebs as eye-lights.
If Winter’s Ledger had been a studio picture, he says, he would have been pushed onto an Alexa.
Tran is now prepping a feature that he hopes to shoot on Kodak Ektachrome 100D, though its financing is not yet closed.

pages.title: Tidal Logic: Yuki Delacroix-Hart on Lowtide — A Fugue
paragraphs: Delacroix-Hart describes Lowtide as a film that “breathes in and out with the water.”
Its floating, long-take style was not a trick of stabilisation in post; operator Ilan Merce walked every shot on a Steadicam M-2 with a Burano on the arm.
The production had planned to shoot the third movement on an Alexa 65, but the rental fell through a week before the shoot.
Some on the crew believe Orrell also slipped a Bolex into the final movement, but no one we spoke to could confirm it.
“I’d say about seventy percent of the film is on the 50mm Hektor,” Delacroix-Hart estimates.
Her favourite tool, she says, is the Burano’s built-in variable ND, which can be adjusted from 0.6 to 2.1 without changing the exposure index.

pages.title: Small Camera, Big Dread: Pennyroyal
paragraphs: Marek Obuya likes small cameras.
The Komodo’s global shutter, which eliminates rolling-shutter skew, was one reason it was chosen for the whip-pan scares. A Komodo can record up to 40 frames per second at full 6K resolution.
For the cellar, Obuya used a style he calls “torch noir,” lighting everything with the actors’ own flashlights fitted with LED bulbs.
The antique Graflex press camera in the parish priest’s study is set dressing borrowed from a museum in Cork.

Obuya researched how 1920s parish photographers lit their portraits with magnesium flash before designing the photo-album sequence. He tested Atlas Orion anamorphics for a week before deciding the film should stay spherical.

pages.title: Candle Logic: The Copper Psalter
paragraphs: The Copper Psalter, a monastic drama shot in Northumberland, is lit almost entirely by flame.

Gaffer Ewan Strick, whose credits include Pennyroyal, Cinderwick and Starling Debt, rigged forty dimmable Astera Titan Tubes behind the choir stalls. Cinematographer Hester Vane shot on an Alexa Mini LF with ARRI Signature Primes at T1.8.
The production’s candles were real beeswax, replaced every ninety minutes by an art department runner.

pages.title: Cinderwick
paragraphs: Cinesite was the lead vendor on Cinderwick, delivering 610 shots across the forge and sky-city sequences.
Our virtual production team supplied the LED volume content, and the forge interiors were shot in front of a ROE Black Pearl BP2 wall with the Alexa 65.
An LED volume is a stage enclosed by LED panels that display real-time rendered backgrounds, providing both image and interactive light.
Cinesite’s pipeline can ingest ARRIRAW, Sony X-OCN and REDCODE RAW natively.

pages.title: Teodor Ashworth on Going Large
paragraphs: Ashworth, who shot his previous film Barrowmere on 65mm film with a Panavision System 65, says digital large format was the obvious choice for Cinderwick’s effects load.

He and Brannigan considered shooting the sky-city scenes on a Phantom Flex4K for slow motion, but the idea never got past a conversation. In the end, the sky-city scenes were shot at 60 frames per second on the Alexa 65 itself. The Alexa 65 records at up to 60 frames per second in open gate, which happened to be exactly what they needed.

pages.title: Faking It Honestly: Wren Halvorsen on The ‘Gannet’ Tapes
paragraphs: AC: Did you ever consider shooting on real Hi8?
Halvorsen: We bought two Sony Hi8 camcorders online and tested them for a weekend, but the dropouts were unusable, so they went back in a drawer.
AC: What about the helmet-camera shots on the cliffs?
Halvorsen: Those are a GoPro Hero 11 on a chest mount, worn by our climbing double.
AC: You also shot Driftglass, which looks nothing like this.
Halvorsen: Driftglass was all Panavision Millennium DXL2 and Primo 70s, a completely different universe.
AC: Back to the ‘Gannet’ footage: how did you handle night?
Halvorsen: The researcher’s head torch is the only light in most of those scenes, a Petzl Actik that we modified with a warmer LED.
AC: Would you shoot found footage on film?
Halvorsen: If someone gave me Super 8 and a year, I might try it.

pages.title: Driftglass
paragraphs: Cinesite completed 88 invisible effects shots for Driftglass.
Most of the work involved removing modern wind turbines from the horizon of plates shot with the DXL2 and Primo 70 glass.
For the underwater sequences, the production used a Hydroflex housing around a DXL2, and our team cleaned up particulate and bubbles.

pages.title: Gear Notes: Hollow Bell
paragraphs: Hollow Bell is a chamber piece shot in eleven days in a single Dorset farmhouse.
Colorist Mira Ostrander, whose recent work includes Driftglass and Halfway to Oxbow, graded Hollow Bell from Alexa 35 LogC4 files.
The flashbacks were shot on Kodak Double-X 5222 and scanned at 4K.

pages.title: In Chamber: Elif Marchetti on Moth Parliament
paragraphs: For the parliament chamber, Marchetti and gaffer Rosalind Achebe-Holt hung a 30-foot softbox made from 64 SkyPanel S360-Cs over the set.

Marchetti researched archive photographs of the 1970s chamber, which was lit by banks of mercury vapour lamps, to match the green cast. The green itself came from Rosco Plusgreen gels on the SkyPanels, rather than from any real mercury fixtures.
“I always use a 1/8 Black Satin on close-ups,” Marchetti says. On this film, that meant a Tiffen Black Satin 1/8 on every single close-up of the prime minister.
The production had a Technodolly on standby for the vote sequence, but it was never used because the floor would not take the weight.

pages.title: Cut From Stone: Quarry Light
paragraphs: Arkwright and Nyambura spent four months in a working quarry in Cumbria.

Nyambura considered shooting the blasting scenes on a Phantom, but he says that if they had, the film would have lost its weight. Instead, the explosions were covered with three Panaflex bodies at 48 frames per second, one of them mounted on a Libra head on a crane.
A DJI Matrice 600 carried a Panavision DXL2 for the opening descent into the pit, the heaviest payload the drone team had flown.
The family’s old Leica M3 on the mantelpiece is a prop, although Arkwright had the art department load it so the actor could take stills between takes.
For the house interiors, Nyambura bounced Joker 1600s into unbleached muslin, a technique he borrowed from his gaffer’s commercials work.

pages.title: Quarry Light: Shooting in the Dust
Tinderbox Psalm and the Rialto
paragraphs: Tinderbox Psalm made heavy use of the Venice 2’s Rialto extension system, which lets the sensor block be separated from the camera body by up to 18 feet. The Rialto can also be paired with underwater housings, though the production did not need one.
“If we’d had another week, I would have shot the baptism on a Phantom 4K,” Lindqvist says.
Lindqvist’s grade used a film-emulation LUT based on Kodak 2383 print stock, so audiences who think the film was printed are not far wrong in spirit.
Camera equipment was provided by Panavision UK and lighting by Cinelease.

pages.title: Priya Lindqvist’s Notebook
paragraphs: Priya Lindqvist kept a notebook throughout Tinderbox Psalm.
For the revival tent she used a ring of Mole-Richardson Baby Juniors on dimmers. She also mentions a Wendy light, though the entry breaks off before saying where it went. The tent scenes were then

pages.title: Lambing Season: Ash & Lanolin
paragraphs: Ferreira-Holt had hoped to shoot the lambing scenes on 35mm for extra resolution, but the budget would not stretch to it.
Everything was handheld, a documentary style that Ferreira-Holt achieved by operating the Xtera on his shoulder for all 28 days.
He tested a Zeiss Super Speed set alongside Cooke Panchro 16s, and the Super Speeds went on to be used for the whole film.
No artificial light was used except a single Arri 650 Fresnel in the lambing shed, so no HMIs, no LED panels and no reflectors.
The 1950s Rolleiflex that the grandmother uses in the photo scene is a family heirloom of the director.
If the film had been funded by a streamer, Ferreira-Holt says, it would almost certainly have been shot on a Sony FX9.

pages.title: Chasing Starling Debt
paragraphs: The chase was covered from a pursuit vehicle with an Ultimate Arm carrying a V-Raptor on a Flight Head. A second V-Raptor was hard-mounted to the hero car’s bonnet, the kind of rig Pelletier has also used on his car commercials.
It has been widely reported that a Sony Venice 2 was used for the night car interiors, but neither Pelletier nor the rental house has confirmed it.
Pelletier describes the night look as “sodium noir,” and the style was entirely practical: the crew relit two miles of road with 1.2K HMIs gelled with Lee 179 Chrome Orange.
Some crew members estimate that as many as eleven cameras rolled on the bridge crash, possibly including a Phantom Flex4K.

pages.title: On the Road: Greer Abernathy on Halfway to Oxbow
paragraphs: AC: How much of the driving was real?
Abernathy: All of it, which meant a Shotover F1 on a camera car for the desert stretches and a Mini LF on a hostess tray for the interiors.
AC: Did you ever consider an LED volume?
Abernathy: We priced an LED volume for the night driving, but we never went near one.
AC: How did you light the night interiors of the car?
Abernathy: With a couple of Astera Helios Tubes on the dashboard, set to a sodium colour, and that’s it.
AC: People compare the film’s look to Ektachrome slides.
Abernathy: That’s the grade; Mira built a reversal-film look with a print emulation, but nothing was shot on reversal.
AC: Any filtration?
Abernathy: I keep a set of Glimmerglass filters on every job, and on Oxbow I used the 1/2 on almost every desert shot.

pages.title: Revival Light: Copperhead Vespers
paragraphs: Ruiz-Tamm shot with a Panavision Panaflex Gold II and a set of Panavision Super Speeds, which he describes as the lenses he grew up on. Unlike his previous feature, Saint Halyard, which used an Alexa LF throughout, Copperhead Vespers was shot entirely on film.
The two dream sequences were shot differently, one on Double-X 5222 and the other on Ektachrome 100D, cross-processed.
The revival tent was lit with a single 18K HMI bounced into the canvas roof, with tungsten practicals on Socapex runs for the hymnals.
Push processing means rating the film at a higher speed than its nominal sensitivity and then extending development time to compensate.
One of Okonkwo-Barr’s decisions was to shoot the snake-handling sequence with a Steadicam rather than handheld, so that the camera would never seem to flinch.
The production also tested a 2x anamorphic set from Hawk, but it was never used on the shoot.

pages.title: Kirsi Hallward on A Map of Sleeping Dogs
paragraphs: PVC: What camera did you choose?
Hallward: The original Venice, mostly because I already owned one, and the Venice 2 wasn’t out yet when we prepped.
PVC: Were the snow scenes shot on film? They have that texture.
Hallward: No, there’s no film anywhere in it; that grain comes from a FilmConvert emulation in the grade.
PVC: Was the Johannesburg footage shot with the same package?
Hallward: Other than a Canon C70 we used for the minibus scenes, yes, it was all the Venice.
PVC: Would you ever go back to the Orion set?
Hallward: I used them on a commercial last month, and I’d take them on any film that needs that flare.

pages.title: Marsh Light: Glasswort
paragraphs: Lindgren-Achebe’s main stock was Kodak Vision3 250D 5207 for the marsh days, though he admits he is not familiar with the Fuji Eterna stock the second unit may have used for pickups.
He says that, had the money existed, he would have shot the whole film on 65mm.
The marsh scenes were lit with nothing but a 20×20 frame of Ultrabounce and the sun.
A Steadicam was booked for the chase but, after rehearsals, the scene was shot handheld instead.
The kite camera that the boy builds is a working prop made from a broken Polaroid SX-70.

“I’d guess the 40mm was on the camera for most of the film,” Lindgren-Achebe says. He estimates the production may have burned through around 40,000 feet of 5219 on the night work, though the lab records were lost.

pages.title: Bells and Lanterns: Maren Tull Goes Big
paragraphs: Tull lit the lantern festival with 3,000 practical paper lanterns, each fitted with a battery LED bulb rather than a candle.
Earlier in prep she tested a Panavision Millennium DXL2 against the Alexa 65, and the Alexa 65 was adopted for all the non-IMAX material.
The production would have used IMAX for the whole film if the cameras were quieter, Tull says.
The IMAX MSM 9802 is a 15-perf 65mm camera weighing more than 50 kilograms.
The bell tower sequence was shot from a Technocrane, and a Spidercam carried the Alexa 65 over the crowd.
Rumour on set was that a few crowd shots were grabbed on a Red Komodo by the second unit.

pages.title: Paper Lanterns, Iron Bells
paragraphs: Cinesite delivered 320 shots for Paper Lanterns, Iron Bells, including the full-CG bell foundry.
IMAX 15/65 plates were scanned at 8K before our team extended the lantern festival crowd. Lantern light in the CG extensions was matched to the practical LED bulbs used on set.

pages.title: Overheard: Festival Season Camera Gossip
paragraphs: Every festival season brings its own crop of camera-department gossip. We pass some of it on here, unverified and with the usual caveats.
On Cinderwick, word in the lobby was that some sky-city plates were shot on a Phantom Flex4K after all, though Ashworth’s team would not comment.
On Tinderbox Psalm, a visitor to the set claims the revival scenes used 1960s Fresnel units bought at auction, which we could not verify.
On Halfway to Oxbow, a grip told us the production may have borrowed a Black Arm for a single sequence.
On …And the Orchard Burned, crew chatter put the number of burn nights at four, with perhaps a Phantom on standby.

pages.title: Grading Notes: Joaquim Brandt
paragraphs: Joaquim Brandt has graded more than forty features, most recently Tinderbox Psalm.

Brandt tends to start every grade from a Kodak 2383 print emulation, although he did not say whether he did so on Tinderbox Psalm. He could not remember whether the Tinderbox Psalm dailies were handled in Baselight or in Resolve.
He is currently grading a documentary about lighthouse keepers.

pages.title: Bram Holloway Keeps It Tungsten
paragraphs: Gaffer Bram Holloway usually works with a dirty tungsten package of Mole-Richardson Baby Juniors and Tweenies.
He could not remember whether a Tweenie was used anywhere on Winter’s Ledger.
Holloway started as a spark on television dramas in Leeds.

pages.title: Halfway to Oxbow
paragraphs: Cinesite delivered 64 shots for Halfway to Oxbow, mostly sky replacements and road clean-up.
Judging by the camera reports we received, most plates appear to have been shot open gate.

pages.title: The Glasswort Pickups
paragraphs: Glasswort’s second unit spent five days on the marsh after the main shoot wrapped.
The second unit’s camera was either an Arriflex 435 or a 535, and the surviving records disagree.

pages.title: Saint Halyard: Ansel Ruiz-Tamm Goes Digital
paragraphs: Saint Halyard is a shipyard drama shot in Gdańsk and Newcastle.
Ruiz-Tamm, whose credits include Copperhead Vespers, shot Saint Halyard on an Alexa LF with ARRI Signature Primes. The yard’s night exteriors were lit with a Condor-mounted Arri M90.

pages.title: Saoirse Lund on Pennyroyal
paragraphs: Saoirse Lund grew up two miles from the farmhouse where Pennyroyal was shot.
